summary: Exhaustive validity audit of every assistant signal/metric: contract + all failure modes per data shape

items.name: buildStressWeek
items.computes: Alerts when ≥3 fixed expenses are due within the next 7 days. Outputs stress-week signal with total amount due and names of first 3+ commitments. Confidence 1.0 (real-time).
items.validityContract: Signal fires deterministically IF AND ONLY IF: (1) at least 3 fixed_expenses exist, (2) each has status !== 'completed', (3) next_due_on is parseable as ISO YYYY-MM-DD, (4) parseFixedExpenseDate returns valid Date (interprets as local-day midnight, not UTC), (5) dueDate >= now AND dueDate <= now+7 days. Gate at L541 prevents firing with < 3 fijos.

For biweekly cycles, 14 days = 2 full cycles (clamped to 1.0). Gate: signals checking confidence < MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) drop if closedDays < 5.6 days (~6 days).

items.name: income-volatility (±10% variance from 3-month avg)

items.name: robust-daily-average (outlier-resistant projection)
items.computes: Median-based daily average ignoring outliers (>3× median or >$50k absolute floor). Falls back to plain mean when <5 days available. Returns {typicalAverage, outlierDaysExcluded, outlierDaysTotal, hadEnoughData}.
inputs: dailyTotals: number[] (discretionary spend per closed day)
items.validityContract: If dailyTotals.length = 0, returns all-zero result. If < 5 days, returns plain mean + hadEnoughData=false. If >= 5 days, computes median, sets threshold=max(median×3, $50k), partitions into typical/outlier. If all days flagged as outliers, falls back to plain mean. Returns typicalAverage >= 0.

sorted = [1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000000]. median = 1000. threshold = max(3000, 50k) = 50k. 1000000 > 50k → outlier. typicalAverage = 4000/4 = 1000. outlierDaysExcluded = 1, outlierDaysTotal = 1000000. Correct.
length === 5, so robust runs. median = 3000, threshold = max(9000, 50k) = 50k. All < 50k. Typical = 3000. Correct.
median = 60000, threshold = max(180000, 50k) = 180000. All 60k < 180k. typicalAverage = 60000. Correct.
sorted.sort() places NaN at end. median = finite value. If NaN is the highest, next-highest is used for median. Arithmetic proceeds. Possible NaN in threshold calc.
Falls back to plainMean. hadEnoughData=true but all were outliers. Returns plain mean as typicalAverage. Correct fallback.

items.recommendedGuard: 1. Guard dailyTotals.length > 0. 2. Filter out NaN/Infinity before sorting (validate all are finite). 3. Ensure median calculation is safe; handle sorted.length = 0. 4. Validate threshold > 0 before comparisons. 5. If typicalCount = 0, mark hadEnoughData=false (not true). 6. Clamp typicalAverage to [0, ∞).

items.name: forecast-7day (pessimistic/baseline/optimistic tracks)
items.computes: Generates 7-day spending forecast under 3 scenarios, adjusted for fixed expenses due and DoW patterns. Each track has {daily[], totalProjected, dailyAvg, endingBalance}. Inflection days flag fixed payments, high-DoW days, and payday proximity.
items.validityContract: Each track clamped to [0, 7] horizon = min(7, diasRestantes). daily[] is 7-element array; values beyond horizon are 0. base function must return ≥ 0 for each day. fixed amounts summed by ISO day. pessimistic uses DoW avg × 1.2 (or baseline if DoW avg=0). endingBalance = remaining - totalProjected (can be negative).

For pessimistic track, validate bucket.avg ≥ 0 and use fallback if 0. 4. parseFixedExpenseDate must not return null for valid dates; skip any null. 5. Fixed amounts must be ≥ 0; clamp to [0, ∞). 6. Daily values must be ≥ 0; enforce with Math.max(0, ...). 7. endingBalance can be negative; don't clamp. 8. Validate inflectionDays array is non-null and sorted.

All detectors return null (gated: length < 10 or < 12). Correct.

failureModes.badOutput: Saturdays.length = 3. Passes gate. Pattern requires 4+ Friday→Sat spikes. If < 4 occurrences, returns null. Correct.

dominanceObs = []. percentile([]) returns 0. catDominanceP75 = max(0.4, 0) = 0.4 (fallback). Correct.

Returns null for catAccelP75. Signal uses hardcoded 1.4. Correct.

failureModes.badOutput: catAccelP75 = max(1.4, 2.25) = 2.25. Correct — user's actual behavior more stringent than default.

failureModes.badOutput: normalizeBreakdownEntries: Number(e.total ?? 0) = 0 for null. Filtered out (amount > 0 check). Safe.

For dominance: require total > 0 before dividing. 5. For accel: require baseline > 0 before ratio. 6. percentile() edge cases: handle values.length = 0 (return 0), values.length = 1 (return values[0]). 7. Clamp final P75 results to min floors (0.4 and 1.4).

items.name: momentum-impact (super-savings-momentum headline sizing)
items.computes: Given a positive-forecast signal, extracts its impactRaw and impactScope, formats as user-facing label with explicit time anchor ('a favor en el ciclo'). Prevents × 12 inflation.

Validate fmt() never produces NaN string; if so, return fallback '$0'. 5. Verify i18n label contains 'ciclo' or 'mes' (audit i18n keys).

Threshold = max(median*3, 50k) (line 71) — absolute floor avoids false positives on tiny-median days. When all days > threshold, falls back to plainMean (line 90-96).

failureModes.badOutput: 800k > 50k, flagged as outlier. typicalAverage=(15+18+12+16+14+13)/6≈14.8k, outlierDaysExcluded=1, outlierTotal=800k. Projection = 14.8k * 28 = 414k (real spend is ~830k over 7 days = 118k/day average). Signals might miss genuine high spending.

items.recommendedGuard: Require closedDays >= 7 before promedioDiario is used in projection (hasReliableProjection gate at control-v2-mock.ts:476 already does this). Require promedioDiario > 0 before division (line 481 checks this). items.name: buildCategoryAcceleration (acceleration signal)
items.computes: When top category this cycle > accelThreshold (1.4× or user's P75) of its 4-week historical avg, fire 'cat-accel' with delta=now-avg.
items.validityContract: Valid when: summaries.length >= 1 (gate line 809), historicalAvg > 0 (gate line 814), byCategory.length >= 1 (implicit via Array.sort). Confidence = rampOneCycle(closedDays) * max(0.5, rampSummaries(summaries.length)) (line 857–859).
